ieltsBandDescription: Mohinga is the undisputed national dish of Myanmar, traditionally relished as a hearty breakfast. It comprises delicate rice vermicelli submerged in a deeply savory broth made from slow-simmered freshwater catfish, intensely infused with lemongrass, ginger, garlic, and cracked black pepper. The soup is thickened with toasted gram flour and studded with tender banana stem discs, then garnished with crispy split-pea fritters, coriander, and a spritz of fresh lime juice.
speakingCueHook: Whenever I am asked to introduce our traditional gastronomy, the first dish that springs to mind is undoubtedly Mohinga, our quintessential breakfast delicacy.

Served with an array of condiments like crispy wonton chips, raw shallot slices, and crushed chili flakes, it offers an impeccable balance of savory creaminess and zesty citrus.
speakingCueHook: If I were to describe my ultimate comfort food, it would unequivocally be Ohn No Khao Swe, a fragrant chicken noodle soup steeped in rich coconut milk.

ieltsBandDescription: Laphet Thoke is Myanmar's most culturally celebrated salad and one of the few dishes worldwide where tea leaves are eaten rather than brewed. Tender green tea leaves undergo months of subterranean lactic fermentation to develop an earthy, tart, and umami complexity. They are tossed with an extraordinary crunchy medley of roasted peanuts, toasted sesame seeds, golden garlic chips, fried split peas, and fresh cabbage.
speakingCueHook: One unique culinary custom in my culture is consuming fermented tea leaves as a savory salad rather than drinking them as a beverage.

It can be served as a soup in a clear fragrant broth or as a dry salad tossed with chili oil, crushed peanuts, and accompanied by crunchy pickled mustard greens.
speakingCueHook: A regional delicacy that has captivated the entire nation is Shan Khao Swe, celebrated for its subtle blend of sweet, sour, and savory notes.

Fresh dace or marine fish is pounded with black peppercorns, garlic, and fresh green chilies to create an intensely piquant broth ladled over delicate vermicelli noodles, contrasted with tamarind pulp and springy fish cakes.
speakingCueHook: For anyone who appreciates unapologetically fiery food, Rakhine Mont Di is an extraordinary example of coastal Myanmar's bold flavors.

It is garnished with boiled egg slices, fish cake ribbons, and deep-fried shallots.
speakingCueHook: One of our most decadent street foods is Nan Gyi Thoke, which combines thick noodles with a velvety chicken curry dressing.

Marinated chicken or tender mutton is layered with fragrant basmati rice, seasoned with saffron, cardamom, cloves, and clarified butter, then baked in sealed pots until tender. It is served with tart mango pickle and fresh mint relish.
speakingCueHook: During significant social gatherings and ceremonies, Danbauk is the centerpiece dish representing celebratory generosity.

ieltsBandDescription: Htamin Thoke exemplifies the Burmese culinary genius of transforming simple leftover steamed rice into a savory masterpiece. Warm rice is tossed by hand with golden garlic oil, roasted chickpea powder, finely pounded dried shrimp, and a touch of tamarind pulp, resulting in an earthy, nutty, and satisfying meal.
speakingCueHook: Htamin Thoke illustrates how everyday pantry staples can be elevated through skilful balancing of garlic oil, gram flour, and dried shrimp.

speakingCueHook: For those who prefer noodle dishes with a thicker, more concentrated sauce, Shwe Taung Khao Swe offers an exceptionally rich coconut chicken reduction.

speakingCueHook: Whenever there is a Buddhist merit-making ceremony or community gathering, Kya Zan Hin Gar is typically served as an elegant, warming soup.

Sliced into ribbons, it is tossed with golden garlic oil, sweet soy sauce, shredded kaffir lime leaves, and toasted peanuts, offering a creamy texture and nutty flavor.
speakingCueHook: A fascinating aspect of Shan cuisine is their unique yellow split-pea tofu, which is completely soy-free and has a wonderfully silky texture.

Liquid yellow split-pea batter is cooked fresh in cauldrons until thick and custardy, then ladled piping hot over a bed of soft rice noodles, topped with seasoned minced pork, red chili oil, and toasted sesame seeds.
speakingCueHook: On cold mornings in the Shan highlands, nothing surpasses a steaming bowl of Tohu Nway, a creamy porridge made from fresh yellow split peas.

ieltsBandDescription: Nga Htamin is a signature Shan culinary creation. Steamed rice is thoroughly kneaded with flaked, seasoned freshwater fish, fragrant turmeric, and garlic oil, then shaped into circular mounds. It is customarily served with crunchy pork cracklings, raw garlic cloves, charred chilies, and pickled Chinese leek roots.
speakingCueHook: Nga Htamin is a remarkable Shan dish that showcases how freshwater fish can be kneaded directly into rice to produce a deeply aromatic meal.

Crispy triangular potato samosas are sliced with scissors into a bowl, drenched in piping-hot, tangy chickpea and tamarind broth, and tossed with finely shredded cabbage, raw shallots, and fragrant mint leaves.
speakingCueHook: One of my absolute favorite evening street snacks is Samusa Thoke, which brilliantly marries crunchy samosas with a tangy, aromatic tamarind broth.

Diners sit around a communal bubbling cauldron on low plastic stools, selecting wooden skewers of braised pork cuts simmered in a light herbal broth. Each bite is plunged into an intensely fiery dipping sauce made from green chilies, garlic, and vinegar.
speakingCueHook: Sitting around a communal pot of Wet Tha Dote Htoe on a bustling pavement provides a vivid glimpse into our sociable urban street culture.

speakingCueHook: Nga Baung Dok highlights the ancient practice of cooking seafood wrapped in banana leaves to preserve moisture and infuse delicate earthy aromas.

speakingCueHook: Talabaw represents the soul of Kayin cuisine, transforming freshly harvested bamboo shoots into a wholesome, comforting herbal soup.

speakingCueHook: The cornerstone of everyday family meals in Myanmar is our signature 'See Pyan' curry, cooked gently until the aromatic seasoned oil rises to the surface.

ieltsBandDescription: Ngapi is the undisputed bedrock of Myanmar's culinary identity, functioning much like miso in Japan or fish sauce in Vietnam. Freshwater fish is pounded with coarse sea salt and allowed to ferment naturally over several months, developing a profound, pungent umami profile that forms the flavor base of soups and dipping sauces.
speakingCueHook: While foreign visitors may initially find its aroma daunting, Ngapi is the indispensable umami foundation that defines authentic Burmese cooking.

speakingCueHook: Hmyin Ngapi is an artisanal shrimp paste from our southern coastlines that imparts an intoxicating savory richness to our curries.

ieltsBandDescription: Myanmar is one of the only nations on Earth where tea leaves are consumed as food. Tender tea flushes are steamed, pressed tightly into bamboo vats or clay pots, and aged underground for months to develop a unique tart and savory astringency.
speakingCueHook: Consuming fermented tea leaves, known locally as Laphet, is deeply embedded in our social fabric as an ancient symbol of hospitality and reconciliation.

ieltsBandDescription: Roselle leaves, known as Chin Baung, are the most beloved sour vegetable in Myanmar. Packed with vitamin C, their natural tartness cuts through rich, oily curries when fried with bamboo shoots and shrimp or simmered in a light, palate-cleansing broth.
speakingCueHook: To balance the richness of our curries, we almost always serve a dish made from Chin Baung, or roselle leaves, prized for their natural tart flavor.

nameMm: မြင်းခွာရွက်
tagline: Nutrient-dense herbal leaves (Centella asiatica) eaten in crunchy salads and medicinal soups.
ingredientsMm: မြင်းခွာရွက်
ieltsBandDescription: Asiatic Pennywort, or Min Kway, is a revered medicinal herb in traditional Burmese wellness. Its slightly bitter, fan-shaped leaves are tossed into a crisp salad with crushed peanuts and sesame, celebrated for cognitive and longevity benefits.
speakingCueHook: Min Kway Ywet is both a delicious salad green and a revered traditional medicinal herb believed to enhance memory and longevity.

nameMm: ကင်းမုံရွက်
tagline: Tender ivy gourd leaves commonly simmered into light, soothing everyday soups (Hin-cho).
burmeseTagline: ကင်းမုံရွက် (ကင်းမုံရွက်ဟင်းချို)
ingredientsEn: Ivy gourd tender leaves and tendrils
ingredientsMm: ကင်းမုံညွန့်
ieltsBandDescription: Ivy gourd leaves are plucked fresh from backyard climbing vines and tossed into a fast-boiling clear soup with garlic and a touch of fish sauce, creating a soothing broth that accompanies daily meals.
speakingCueHook: A typical home-cooked Burmese dinner invariably features a light vegetable soup such as Kin Mon Ywet to aid digestion.

nameMm: ပဲပုပ်
tagline: Sun-dried fermented soybean discs toasted over coals to provide deep smoky umami in Shan dishes.
ingredientsMm: ပဲပုပ်စေ့
ieltsBandDescription: Pe Poke represents the genius of highland food preservation in Shan and Kachin States. Fermented soybeans are pounded into thin round discs and sun-dried; when toasted over glowing charcoal, they puff up and impart an irresistible smoky, savory depth to soups and stir-fries.
speakingCueHook: In Shan cuisine, sun-dried fermented soybean discs called Pe Poke are charred over glowing coals to yield an extraordinarily smoky umami aroma.

tagline: Finely roasted yellow split-pea flour used to thicken broths, bind noodle salads, and make fritters.
burmeseTagline: ကုလားပဲမှုန့် (မုန့်ဟင်းခါးနှင့် အသုပ်များတွင် မရှိမဖြစ်)
ieltsBandDescription: Roasted chickpea flour, or Pe Hmont, is an essential binder and thickener across Burmese cuisine. It lends body to the national dish Mohinga, gives salads a nutty coating, and forms the crispy batter for traditional fritters.
speakingCueHook: Toasted gram flour is a cornerstone of our culinary technique, functioning simultaneously as a soup thickener and a nutty salad dressing.

nameMm: ဒန့်ဒလွန်သီး
tagline: Moringa tree drumstick pods simmered in aromatic sour soups and yellow split-pea dhal.
burmeseTagline: ဒန့်ဒလွန်သီး (ဒန့်ဒလွန်သီးဟင်းချို / ချဉ်ရည်ဟင်း)
ingredientsMm: ဒန့်ဒလွန်သီး
ieltsBandDescription: The long, ridged pods of the Moringa tree, called Dandalun Thee, are chopped into finger-length sections and simmered in sour fish curries or dhal. Diners chew the fibrous pods to extract the sweet, succulent inner pulp and seeds.
speakingCueHook: Dandalun Thee, or drumstick pods, are a cherished addition to our sour broths, offering both remarkable health benefits and a sweet vegetal flavor.

nameMm: စပါးလင်
tagline: Citrusy, fibrous stalks bruised and tied in knots to eliminate fishiness and perfume broths.
burmeseTagline: စပါးလင် (မုန့်ဟင်းခါးနှင့် ငါးဟင်းများတွင် မရှိမဖြစ်)
ingredientsMm: စပါးလင်တံ
ieltsBandDescription: Lemongrass stalks are bruised with a pestle and tied into neat knots before being plunged into boiling fish broths and curries. It neutralizes marine gaminess while perfuming dishes with an uplifting citrus bouquet.
speakingCueHook: Lemongrass is vital in our fish cooking, where its crushed stalks release bright citrus essential oils that mask any residual muddy notes.

nameMm: နနွင်းမှုန့်
tagline: Golden turmeric root powder; the natural colorant, preservative, and antiseptic foundation of all curries.
ingredientsMm: နနွင်းတက်
ieltsBandDescription: Turmeric is omnipresent in Burmese households. Virtually all meats and seafood are rubbed with turmeric powder before cooking, not solely for its warm earthy flavor and golden radiance, but for its ancient antimicrobial and preservative qualities in a tropical climate.
speakingCueHook: In Burmese cooking, almost every raw meat or fish is pre-marinated with golden turmeric powder for both hygiene and vibrant color.

nameEn: Kyet Thun Ni & Kyet Thun Phyu (Shallots & Garlic)
nameMm: ကြက်သွန်နီ / ကြက်သွန်ဖြူ
tagline: Red shallots and pungent garlic; the indispensable aromatic twin pillars of Burmese savory cuisine.
burmeseTagline: ကြက်သွန်နီနှင့် ကြက်သွန်ဖြူ (မြန်မာ့ဟင်းချက်အနှစ်၏ အခြေခံ)
ingredientsMm: ကြက်သွန်နီ
ကြက်သွန်ဖြူ
ieltsBandDescription: Shallots and garlic are finely pounded with ginger and turmeric to create the 'Hsa-nwin Kyet-thun' paste that forms the base of almost every curry and soup in Myanmar, giving body, sweetness, and deep savory richness.
speakingCueHook: The very aroma of shallots and garlic sizzling slowly in peanut oil is what every Burmese person instantly associates with home.

nameEn: Kyet Thun Phyu Si Gyaw (Crispy Garlic & Garlic Oil)
nameMm: ကြက်သွန်ဖြူဆီချက်
tagline: Slow-fried golden garlic slivers and infused fragrant oil; the universal dressing for noodles and salads.
burmeseTagline: ကြက်သွန်ဖြူဆီချက် (အသုပ်နှင့် ခေါက်ဆွဲများအတွက်)
ingredientsMm: ကြက်သွန်ဖြူ
မြေပဲဆီ
နနွင်းအနည်းငယ်
ieltsBandDescription: Garlic oil is Myanmar's universal condiment. Sliced garlic is fried gently in peanut oil until golden and crunchy; the strained garlic chips provide crunch while the fragrant, infused golden oil is drizzled generously over salads and noodle bowls.
speakingCueHook: A drizzle of golden fried garlic oil is the secret touch that ties together almost every noodle dish and salad in our cuisine.

nameMm: မန်ကျည်းမှည့်
tagline: Aged, sun-dried tamarind pulp soaked in water to yield a fruity, thirst-quenching sour nectar.
burmeseTagline: မန်ကျည်းမှည့် (ဟင်းချိုနှင့် အသုပ်များအတွက် အချဉ်ရည်)
ingredientsMm: မန်ကျည်းသီးမှည့်
ieltsBandDescription: Tamarind pulp provides the clean, fruity acidity favored in Burmese dishes over vinegar. Mixed with warm water and strained, its velvety tart juice enlivens noodle broths, cuts through oily curries, and serves as the dipping sauce base for street fritters.
speakingCueHook: Rather than relying on artificial vinegar, we use soaked tamarind pulp to give our soups and dressings a naturally refreshing, fruity tang.

nameMm: ထန်းလျက်
tagline: Unrefined golden-brown palm sugar cakes tapped from upper Myanmar's majestic toddy palms.
burmeseTagline: ထန်းလျက် (အညာဒေသထွက် သဘာဝထန်းလျက်ခဲ)
ingredientsEn: Boiled sap of the Asian palmyra toddy palm
ingredientsMm: ထန်းရည်ချို
ieltsBandDescription: Tapped from wild toddy palm trees that define the arid landscapes of Bagan and Upper Myanmar, Htanyet is pure, unrefined palm sugar. Small round cakes flavored with ginger, coconut, or plum are eaten after meals with green tea to stimulate digestion.
speakingCueHook: At the conclusion of a traditional Burmese meal, guests are offered small cakes of toddy palm jaggery alongside hot green tea to aid digestion.

nameMm: ငါးငံပြာရည်
tagline: Clear amber fermented fish sauce; the primary savory salt seasoning of Myanmar home cooking.
burmeseTagline: ငါးငံပြာရည် (ဟင်းခတ်ဆားရည်)
ieltsBandDescription: Clear, savory, and rich in natural glutamates, Nga Pyar Yay is the liquid salt of Myanmar. It imparts an immediate depth of savoriness to soups, curries, and table dressings without muting other delicate herbal aromatics.
speakingCueHook: Nga Pyar Yay is the fundamental savory seasoning in our kitchens, contributing vital umami without masking the freshness of local herbs.

nameMm: ဘာလချောင်
tagline: Crispy dried shrimp relish pan-fried with shallots, garlic chips, and fiery red chili flakes.

ငရုတ်သီးမှုန့်
ဆီချက်
ieltsBandDescription: Balachaung is an explosive condiment of crunchy fried shallots, garlic, and shredded sun-dried prawns tossed with red chili flakes. Packed into glass jars, a single spoonful sprinkled over plain steamed rice elevates a humble meal into a feast.
speakingCueHook: For Burmese students living abroad, a jar of Balachaung is the ultimate taste of home that instantly rescues any plain bowl of rice.

tagline: Crisp golden street-side fritters of bottle gourd, yellow split-peas, onions, and Shan tofu.
ingredientsMm: ပဲဝါခြမ်း
မုန့်နှစ်
မန်ကျည်းဆော့စ်
ieltsBandDescription: A Kyaw Sone embodies the vibrant street teatime culture of Myanmar. Food vendors in morning markets dip sweet bottle gourd strips, yellow split-pea patties, and tofu slices in light rice batter, deep-frying them in large iron woks until shatteringly crisp, served with sweet-and-sour tamarind dip.
speakingCueHook: Teahouse culture in Myanmar revolves around hot sweet milk tea paired with a platter of freshly fried A Kyaw Sone fritters.

nameEn: Mont Lin Ma Ya (Twin Batter Cakes)
nameMm: မုန့်လင်မယား

burmeseTagline: မုန့်လင်မယား (ဘဲဥ/ကြက်ဥ၊ ပဲပြုတ်၊ ကြက်သွန်မြိတ်)

ieltsBandDescription: Known poetically as 'Husband and Wife Cakes', this street delicacy consists of two crispy hemispherical rice cakes cooked in special dimpled cast-iron pans. One half is filled with a whole quail egg and the other with boiled garden peas, bonded together while cooking into a single bite.
speakingCueHook: A charming example of our street food naming tradition is Mont Lin Ma Ya, which couples two crispy rice cakes with quail eggs into a single bite.

nameMm: ရွှေရင်အေး
tagline: Refreshing chilled coconut milk dessert loaded with pandan jelly, sago, sweet sticky rice, and white bread.
ingredientsEn: Sweet purple or white sticky rice

ieltsBandDescription: Literally translating to 'golden heart cooler', Shwe Yin Aye is the ultimate antidote to the scorching tropical afternoon heat. A bowl of sweetened, fragrant coconut milk is piled high with pandan jelly droplets, chewy sago pearls, sweet sticky rice, and a slice of white bread that absorbs the coconut cream.
speakingCueHook: To beat the sweltering heat of our dry season, nothing is more therapeutic than a chilled bowl of Shwe Yin Aye packed with pandan jelly and coconut cream.

nameMm: ဆနွင်းမကင်း
tagline: Baked golden semolina cake enriched with coconut cream, clarified butter (ghee), and poppy seeds.

ieltsBandDescription: Sanwin Makin is a rich, dense traditional confection made by cooking semolina grains with coconut milk, sugar, and clarified butter, then baking the mixture until the surface caramelizes into a deep golden crust crowned with toasted white poppy seeds.
speakingCueHook: Sanwin Makin is our premier baked confection, characterized by its golden crust, fragrant coconut milk, and crunch of toasted poppy seeds.

tagline: Sweet glutinous rice dumplings stuffed with palm jaggery, famously eaten during the Thingyan Water Festival.
ingredientsMm: ထန်းလျက်ခဲ
အုန်းသီးဆံ
ရေနွေးဆူဆူ
ieltsBandDescription: Meaning 'dumplings that float on water', this sweet is synonymous with the annual Thingyan New Year Water Festival. Chewy glutinous rice dough balls are filled with dark palm jaggery nuggets; when boiled, they float to the surface upon being cooked, then rolled in freshly grated coconut.
speakingCueHook: During our lively Thingyan Water Festival in April, communities gather on the streets to roll and boil Mont Lone Yay Paw dumplings together.

nameMm: ဘိန်းမုန့်
tagline: Fluffy, honeycomb-textured street pancake sweetened with palm molasses and topped with poppy seeds.

ထန်းလျက်ရည်

ဗာဒံစေ့
ieltsBandDescription: Bein Mont is a beloved Burmese street pancake cooked in heavy lidded cast-iron pans over glowing embers. The fermented rice batter rises into a spongy, honeycomb texture sweetened with dark palm jaggery and studded with crunchy coconut slivers and poppy seeds.
speakingCueHook: Walking past morning markets, the intoxicating aroma of Bein Mont pancakes baking over charcoal embers is an unforgettable sensory experience.

nameMm: နှမ်းမရွက်
tagline: Earthy, aromatic perilla / wild sesame leaves tossed into rustic salads and sour fish broths.
burmeseTagline: နှမ်းမရွက် (နှမ်းမရွက်သုပ် / ဟင်းချို)
ingredientsMm: နှမ်းမရွက်
ieltsBandDescription: Perilla leaves, or Hnan Ma Ywet, are wild aromatic greens with serrated edges and an earthy anise-mint bouquet. Common in upper Myanmar and Shan State, they are tossed with roasted peanut powder or simmered with river fish to add distinct herbal complexity.
speakingCueHook: In upper Myanmar, Hnan Ma Ywet or perilla leaves are favored for their distinct herbal fragrance in fresh vegetable salads.

nameMm: ပင်စိမ်း
tagline: Pungent holy basil leaves providing a peppery, clove-like aromatic lift to chicken curries and bamboo soups.
ingredientsMm: ပင်စိမ်းရွက်
ieltsBandDescription: Unlike sweet Italian basil, Burmese holy basil carries an intense peppery and clove-like profile. Tossed in at the very end of cooking, it enlivens rich chicken stir-fries and traditional Kayin bamboo shoot broths.
speakingCueHook: Holy basil is our go-to aromatic herb when we want to add an invigorating, peppery lift to rich poultry dishes.

nameMm: နံနံပင်
tagline: Crisp cilantro herb used universally as an aromatic cooling garnish over piping-hot noodle soups.
burmeseTagline: နံနံပင် (ဟင်းရည်နှင့် အသုပ်များအတွက် အုပ်မွှေး)
ingredientsEn: Fresh coriander leaves and tender stems
ingredientsMm: နံနံပင်
ieltsBandDescription: Fresh cilantro is the universal herbal garnish in Myanmar. Chopped generously, its vibrant citrus notes cut through rich fish broths like Mohinga and add fresh herbaceous crunch to noodle salads.
speakingCueHook: No bowl of Burmese noodle soup is complete without a generous handful of fresh cilantro scattered on top.

nameMm: ငရုတ်ကောင်း
tagline: Coarsely crushed black peppercorns delivering dry, floral heat in traditional medicinal broths (Hin-gar).
burmeseTagline: ငရုတ်ကောင်း (ဟင်းခါးနှင့် စွပ်ပြုတ်ရည်များအတွက်)
ingredientsMm: ငရုတ်ကောင်းစေ့
ieltsBandDescription: Before the introduction of chili peppers from the Americas, black pepper was the primary source of fiery heat in ancient Burma. It remains the signature spice in peppery clear broths designed to soothe colds and stimulate perspiration.
speakingCueHook: When recovering from a cold, Burmese grandmothers always prepare a bowl of clear broth spiked heavily with crushed black pepper.

nameEn: Hnan & Hnan Si (Sesame Seeds & Sesame Oil)
tagline: Toasted white and black sesame seeds and artisanal cold-pressed sesame oil from the central dry zone.
ingredientsMm: နှမ်းဆီစစ်စစ်
ieltsBandDescription: Myanmar is one of the world's leading producers of sesame. Toasted sesame seeds add a pleasant nutty crunch to salads and desserts, while pure cold-pressed sesame oil is drizzled raw over breakfast rice and noodles for an intense, roasty perfume.
speakingCueHook: Myanmar's dry zone produces exceptional sesame, which we cold-press into a deeply fragrant oil that perfumes our breakfast noodles.

nameEn: Mye Pe & Mye Pe Si (Peanuts & Peanut Oil)
tagline: Golden crushed roasted peanuts and unrefined fragrant peanut oil; the culinary lifeblood of Burmese curries.
burmeseTagline: မြေပဲလှော်နှင့် မြေပဲဆီစစ်စစ်
ingredientsMm: မြေပဲဆီ
ieltsBandDescription: Unrefined peanut oil is the gold standard cooking medium in Myanmar, offering a high smoke point and distinct nutty sweetness. Crushed roasted peanuts are added to nearly every salad, providing textural contrast and healthy fats.
speakingCueHook: The secret to our curries' depth lies in cooking aromatics slowly in pure, fragrant peanut oil produced in the central plains.

tagline: Mild, succulent bottle gourd; Myanmar's premier vegetable for crispy fritters and cooling sour broths.
ieltsBandDescription: With its high water content and tender sponge-like flesh, bottle gourd easily absorbs the flavors of dried shrimp, tamarind, and garlic in sour broths, and transforms into crispy golden tempura fritters when battered and fried.
speakingCueHook: Bottle gourd is beloved across Myanmar, whether deep-fried into crispy teatime fritters or boiled in refreshing sour soups.

nameMm: ကောက်ညှင်း
tagline: Sweet, fragrant glutinous rice (white, purple, and red varieties); the foundation of festival confections.
ingredientsEn: Glutinous sweet rice grains (Oryza sativa var. glutinosa)
ingredientsMm: ကောက်ညှင်းဆန်
ieltsBandDescription: Steamed with toasted sesame seeds and shredded fresh coconut, sticky rice is the heart of Myanmar's morning street food and ceremonial confections. Varieties range from fragrant white sticky rice to heirloom deep-purple Ngacheik rice.
speakingCueHook: Steamed sticky rice topped with roasted sesame and shredded coconut is our time-honored traditional breakfast on chilly mornings.

nameMm: ငါးဖယ်
tagline: Springy, bouncy freshwater fish paste whipped with saltwater into cakes and curry balls.
burmeseTagline: ငါးဖယ်ခြစ် (ငါးဖယ်ကြော် / ငါးဖယ်ဟင်း)

ဆားရည်
ieltsBandDescription: Nga Phe is revered for its extraordinary natural elasticity. Skilled cooks scrape the firm white flesh of the featherback fish from its bones and beat it rhythmically against a wooden mortar with saltwater until it forms a springy, bouncy paste with zero additives.
speakingCueHook: Achieving the perfect springy bounce in Nga Phe fish cakes requires vigorous hand-kneading against a wooden mortar.

nameMm: မုန်ညင်းချဉ်
tagline: Tangy, crunchy mustard greens lacto-fermented with rice water, salt, and red bird's-eye chili.
burmeseTagline: မုန်ညင်းချဉ် (ရှမ်းခေါက်ဆွဲနှင့် တွဲဖက်စားစရာ)

ငရုတ်သီးစိမ်း
ieltsBandDescription: Lacto-fermented using the starch in rice-washing water, Mon Nyin Chin provides a crisp, sour, and mildly pungent counterpoint that cuts through the savory richness of Shan noodles and pork curries.
speakingCueHook: Mon Nyin Chin, or pickled mustard greens, provides the crucial sour crunch that balances the savory richness of our noodle dishes.

nameMm: ပုဇွန်ခြောက်
tagline: Premium sun-dried sea prawns; pounded into savory golden dust to add sweetness and umami to salads.
burmeseTagline: ပုဇွန်ခြောက် (ပုဇွန်ခြောက်မှုန့် / အသုပ်များတွင် မရှိမဖြစ်)
ingredientsMm: ပုဇွန်ခြောက်
ieltsBandDescription: Sun-dried prawns are a prized luxury condiment in Burmese kitchens. Pounded into a fine golden fluff, they provide a burst of natural sea sweetness and concentrated umami to salads and dipping sauces.
speakingCueHook: A spoonful of pounded dried shrimp powder instantly infuses any vegetable salad with an intense burst of coastal umami.

tagline: Piquant, warming ginger root pounded with garlic to eliminate gaminess and stimulate appetite.
ingredientsMm: ချင်းတက်
ieltsBandDescription: Fresh ginger is an essential aromatic root in Myanmar. Beyond forming the holy curry triad with garlic and shallots, finely shredded pickled ginger is the star of Gin Thoke, a zesty palate-cleansing salad.
speakingCueHook: Fresh ginger is not only a vital aromatic in our curries, but also the star ingredient in our refreshing pickled ginger salad.

nameMm: မုန့်လက်ဆောင်း
tagline: Chilled beverage of green rice-flour drops submerged in toasted sesame jaggery syrup and coconut milk.
burmeseTagline: မုန့်လက်ဆောင်း (ထန်းလျက်ရည် / အုန်းနို့)

ieltsBandDescription: Mont Latt Saung is an ancient refreshing drink sold by itinerant street vendors. Soft, green pandan rice drops are ladled into a glass, bathed in rich caramelized palm jaggery syrup or coconut milk, and finished with fragrant toasted sesame seeds.
speakingCueHook: When the summer sun becomes unbearable, street stalls serving iced Mont Latt Saung in dark palm syrup are a welcome oasis.

nameMm: ထမနဲ

Teams of strong men vigorously stir huge woks of sticky rice with wooden oars, incorporating roasted peanuts, sesame seeds, coconut slivers, and ginger into a chewy, nutty delicacy offered to monks and neighbors.
speakingCueHook: Htamane festival in February is a marvelous communal spectacle where whole communities come together to stir giant woks of festive sticky rice.

ieltsBandDescription: Htoe Mont is Mandalay's most prestigious royal confectionery. Sticky rice is continuously kneaded and reduced with rich butter, sugar, and toasted nuts until it becomes a glossy, chewy confection packed into traditional bamboo gift boxes.
speakingCueHook: Whenever people return from a trip to Mandalay, they invariably bring back boxes of Htoe Mont, a royal sticky rice confection loaded with cashews and ghee.

nameMm: ဟာလဝါ (ပုသိမ်ဟာလဝါ)
tagline: Pathein's signature sticky rice fudge baked with coconut cream, ghee, and poppy seeds in banana bark boxes.
